summary.text: A previously healthy 45-year-old man presented to the emergency room after 4 days of high fever and dry cough, with severe shortness of breath, nausea, vomiting and clammy cold extremities. Examination showed bilateral wet rales and a regular but fast heart rate. ECG at presentation showed sinus tachycardia with complete right bundle branch block, and chest CT showed diffuse bilateral patchy infiltrates and ground-glass opacity.

A presumptive diagnosis of fulminant myocarditis with cardiogenic shock was made, and oxygen, dobutamine, norepinephrine, a diuretic, empiric imipenem and vancomycin, IVIG, vitamin C and coenzyme Q 10 were started without steroids or immunosuppressants. Etiologic PCR and serology tests were all negative, and biopsy was not performed.

With no improvement he was transferred to the EICU, where intubation, VA-ECMO and CRRT were started 6 hours after EICU admission. Transthoracic echocardiography showed global hypokinesia and an EF of 18%. He then had short ventricular tachycardia and, 2 days later, refractory VT and ventricular fibrillation; IABP was added after bedside echocardiography showed LVEF below 10%, and atrial fibrillation followed IABP support.

Cardiac contractility improved on daily echocardiography; ECMO was withdrawn on hospital day 11, IABP on day 14, and he was extubated on day 20 but required tracheotomy. After a 33-day EICU stay he was discharged on day 81 with normal laboratory tests and sinus rhythm with complete right bundle branch block; the stay was complicated by pneumonia, acute renal failure, gastrointestinal bleeding and critical illness myopathy.

Only the qualitative laboratory statements in the text are recorded, so no per-analyte or per-day numeric laboratory series is annotated. Nothing is inferred from the image values.

evidence.quote: Laboratory measurements showed thrombocytopenia, elevated levels of cardiac enzyme, liver enzyme, blood urea nitrogen, creatinine, and inflammatory markers (Table 1).

ambiguities.issue: The abstract gives transthoracic echocardiogram and the medical history as the basis of the presumptive diagnosis, whereas the case text reports the echocardiogram after VA-ECMO initiation. Basis wording does not order events; no order is inferred.

evidence.quote: Transthoracic echocardiogram and the medical history showed presumptive diagnosis was fulminant myocarditis with cardiogenic shock.
A transthoracic echocardiogram (TTE) showed global hypokinesia and severely impaired left ventricular (LV) function with an ejection fraction (EF) of 18%.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says electrical storm occurred twice during ECMO support, while the case text describes short VT, then refractory VT and VF 2 days later, and calls only the latter an electrical storm that could not be reversed. The source does not map the two storms to these episodes, so the abstract statement is its own event, and its treatment with IABP is not ordered against the refractory episode.

evidence.quote: He experienced electrical storm twice during ECMO support
However, he experienced refractory VT and ventricular fibrillation (VF) 2 days later.

ambiguities.issue: The abstract states ECMO and IABP were continued for 11 and 14 days while the text gives hospital day 11 and 14 for withdrawal; the start day of each device is not stated, so the durations and hospital days are kept as separate statements without reconciling them.

evidence.quote: ECMO and IABP were continued for 11 and 14 days respectively.
ECMO was able to be withdrawn on hospital day 11

ambiguities.issue: The sentence setting the initial flow rate to 4.5 L/min does not name the device; it is kept as a review-only fact and not attached to ECMO.

evidence.quote: To recover from peripheral circulatory failure, the initial flow rate was set as 4.5 L/min.

ambiguities.issue: The text reports echocardiography with normal chambers, normal wall motion and EF 67% after the discharge sentence but gives no time for it. The image-only Table 1 prints its EF values in day columns (pixel content, visual.json only), so no time is assigned and the echocardiogram is not placed in the discharge event.

evidence.quote: Echocardiography showed normal cardiac chambers and normal wall motion with EF 67%.

ambiguities.issue: The text gives an estimated LVEF of 50% on TEE on hospital day 11, while the image-only Table 1 prints a different EF entry under D11. Image values are pixel content only, so the text value is kept review-only and no table value is used.

evidence.quote: ECMO was able to be withdrawn on hospital day 11 when transesophageal echocardiogram (TEE) showed estimated LVEF of 50%

ambiguities.issue: The abstract says ECMO was initiated immediately after admission, while the case text says VA-ECMO was initiated 6 hours after EICU admission following transfer from the ER in 12 hours. The statements use different anchors and are not reconciled; the event keeps the case-text time.

evidence.quote: The patient's condition deteriorated drastically and ECMO was initiated immediately after admission.
tracheal intubation, VA-ECMO, and continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) were initiated 6 hours after EICU admission

Figure 1
Electrocardiograms during the clinical course. A, ECG at presentation showed sinus tachycardia, complete right bundle branch block, and diffuse ST-segment elevation. D, ECG at the time of discharge showed sinus rhythm with complete right bundle branch block. ECMO = extracorporeal membrane oxygenation, IABP = intra-aortic balloon pumping, ECG = electrocardiogram.
